A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM training experiments, AIME evaluations, stability and clipping analyses, and additional reasoning-task experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds RLHF reward curves, AlpacaEval results, threshold sensitivity experiments, and a Top-K probability-mass analysis.

M1.justification: The DPPO objective, asymmetric divergence-based mask, rollout-policy anchor, and Binary/Top-K TV and KL approximations remain unchanged. Section 4 expands their explanation without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G.1 add open-ended alignment training on UltraFeedback and HH-RLHF and evaluation on AlpacaEval 2.0. This substantially extends the retained mathematical, abstract, induction, and multi-turn reasoning coverage to learned-reward alignment.

E2.justification: The existing algorithmic comparators are retained. New Table 2 additionally evaluates the initial Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 model as an explicit reference alongside GRPO and DPPO fine-tuning. The new GRPO clipping configurations are setting variations rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: The added RLHF experiments introduce Gemma-2-9B-It and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B. AlpacaEval adds length-controlled/raw win rates and response length, using the step-150 checkpoint. Appendix G.4 adds an 8k-context threshold sweep; the original experiments' Table 1 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.4 adds a focused sensitivity study of DPPO divergence thresholds and GRPO clipping ranges. Appendix C.1 adds tracking of top-20 probability mass during RLHF to assess approximation fidelity. The earlier stability, clipping-direction, and Binary-versus-Top-K analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained Avg@32 evaluation and Gaussian smoothing practices are unchanged; the shaded unsmoothed traces are not uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial RLHF and AlpacaEval results. Table 2 reports length-controlled/raw win rates of 80.90/79.93 for DPPO, 77.05/72.20 for GRPO, and 59.39/69.38 for the initial model. Threshold-sensitivity and probability-mass findings are also new. The earlier experimental curves are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: The bounds and proofs are retained: the average-divergence bound promoted into Theorem 3.2 already appears in v1 Appendix B.3. Section 4.3 adds a mathematical assertion that substituting D = r_t - 1 recovers PPO. As written, this signed expression cannot reproduce lower-ratio clipping for a positive threshold.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about ratio-clipping bias, DPPO, finite-horizon guarantees, and improved stability and efficiency. The added experiments support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 extends the interpretation to noisy learned-reward optimization and external alignment performance. Appendix G.1 newly acknowledges reward hacking: later checkpoints earn higher rewards but lower AlpacaEval scores. New discussions also interpret threshold robustness and increasing Top-K probability coverage.

D1.justification: v2 supplies reward-model identification and checkpoint-selection information for RLHF, plus the 8k context and explicit threshold grids for the sensitivity study. Existing implementation details and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged. The repository link is relocated, not newly provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for HH-RLHF, UltraFeedback, Gemma 2, Skywork-Reward, Li et al. (2026), and Qi et al. (2024). These support new experiments or revised attributions; Appendix A's substantive positioning relative to earlier trust-region and mismatch research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and parts of Sections 4 and 5 are rewritten, the existing average-divergence guarantee is integrated into the main theorem, and Appendix G gains new subsections. Terminology and publication-header edits are limited; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 removes the opening overview graphic and brings the existing mismatch scatterplot onto the first page. It adds RLHF curves, a probability-mass diagnostic, a six-panel sensitivity figure, and AlpacaEval Table 2. These materially expand the visual evidence, while the earlier experimental plots are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The RLHF and AlpacaEval evaluations broaden empirical support beyond verifiable reasoning, while sensitivity checks and the reward-hacking qualification improve practical assessment. These are useful additions to an already extensive study. The gains are tempered by limited RLHF protocol and uncertainty reporting, the new PPO-recovery sign error, and a leaderboard-wide SOTA claim that Table 2 alone does not establish.
